data.title: Campaign Objective Assessed as Strategic Rather Than Opportunistic
data.summary:
The campaign's shape — sustained duration, consistent framing, and investment in assets
built before the first post — indicates a planned objective rather than opportunistic
piling-on after a news event.
data.description:
The distinction decides the response. An opportunistic pile-on decays on its own and is
usually made worse by engagement. A campaign with a strategic objective does not decay,
because somebody is paying to sustain it, and ignoring it concedes the field.

Indicators of planning include assets created well before they were used, a narrative
that survives being debunked by changing its supporting claim while keeping its
conclusion, and continued investment after the originating news cycle has closed.

State the assessed objective explicitly and separately from the evidence for it. An
objective is the most consequential and least verifiable thing in the report, and a
reader must be able to see which parts are observation and which are inference.
data.recommendation:
* Plan for a campaign that persists: a single rebuttal is the wrong instrument against a
  sustained operation.
* Agree in advance the threshold at which the client escalates — to platforms, to a
  regulator, or to law enforcement — so the decision is not made under pressure.
* Re-assess the objective as the campaign adapts; the first assessment is frequently
  incomplete.
data.short_recommendation: Plan for persistence, and set escalation thresholds in advance.
